messages.subject: Using row/column-wise a function that needs external variable
messages.subject_clean: Using row/column-wise a function that needs external variable
messages.body_plain:
Hi

Somehow my problem does not seem too complicated, but I was not able to find a clean solution, but I am sure there is a solution for this in Hadley's toolbox :-)

So what I want to do is just a t.test on every column of a dataset (so colwise) and then for subgroups (rowise, with ddply). The problem is that each time I need to access the "external" variable defining the treatment, and it seems difficult to do this with colwise(), as it specifically focuses on a single variable each time.

In other words:

## The data frame, a treatment variable, a subgroup variable,
# and two variables to check for
df <- data.frame(treatment=rep(c(TRUE, FALSE),each=10),
                 gender=rep(c("M", "F"), 10), Var1=rnorm(20),Var2=rnorm(20))

# simplest manual outcome is:
t.test(Var1~treatment, data=df)$p.val

## Now want to do for each Variable (Var1, var2,...) and for subgroups (male vs female)

library(plyr)

#does not work
numcolwise(function(x) t.test(x~treatment)$p.val)(df)

# so solution I found is:
numcolwise(function(x) t.test(x~df$treatment)$p.val)(df)

## but how to generalise to ddply?
ddply(df, .(gender), numcolwise(function(x) t.test(x~treatment)))

Do you see any simple way to do this? Sorry if I missed something!!

Thanks a lot

Matthieu

DF <- melt(df, id = c("treatment", "gender"))
f <- function(d) t.test(value ~ treatment, data = d)$p.val
ddply(DF, .(gender, variable), f)

messages.subject: Confusing interaction between reshape and reshape2: melt(data.frame, value.name='a')
messages.subject_clean: Confusing interaction between reshape and reshape2: melt(data.frame, value.name='a')
messages.body_plain:
I've been using the variable.name <http://variable.name> and value.name <http://value.name> arguments a lot
lately.  I think they make code a lot cleaner.
In the past, I've had some issues with both reshape and reshape2 being
loaded and the wrong melt getting used. I've resolved these by
removing the reshape package, but now I'm now using a package that
requires reshape (GGally), so this "simple" solution no longer works.

I figured I'd just make *sure* the correct function gets called using
the reshape2::melt() syntax.  I'm getting some strange results that I
don't really understand, though.  I can use a full
reshape2:::melt.data.frame() call to get the desired results, but this
seems like the Wrong Way (tm).  Any insight would be great.  (I have
fresh installs of both packages, R version 3.0.1, ubuntu).

## If I comment out this line, all 3 work fine
require(reshape)
require(reshape2)
##
head(melt(ChickWeight, id=2:4, value.name <http://value.name>='a'), 5)
##  Doesn't work, no errors, mystery!
head(reshape2::melt(ChickWeight, id=2:4, value.name <http://value.name>='a'), 5)
## works
head(reshape2:::melt.data.frame(ChickWeight, id=2:4, value.name <http://value.name>='a'), 5)

Thanks,
Christian
--

messages.subject: odd interaction between quantile and ddply
messages.subject_clean: odd interaction between quantile and ddply
messages.body_plain:
I've been working with some code to calculate quantiles when summarising in plyr, and keep getting odd results.  Here's my sample code - why are the quantiles coming out to be the same as the mean?

mono <- 8

n <- 8

adf <- data.frame(sp = sort(rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H", "Poly"), n)),

div = c(rep(1,mono*n), rep(mono,n)))

#we sample some compositional effect from a random distribution for ALL treatments

adf$compEffect <- 3*as.vector(replicate(mono+1, rep(rnorm(1), n)))

adf$y <- adf$compEffect + rnorm(nrow(adf), adf$div)

adfSummarized <- ddply(adf, c("sp", "div"), summarise, y = mean(y), ymin = quantile(y, 0.025), ymax = quantile(y, 0.975))

This yields the following.  Why are all three columns the same value?  They shouldn't be.

> adfSummarized

    sp div          y       ymin       ymax

1    A   1  3.2404933  3.2404933  3.2404933

2    B   1 -1.4406893 -1.4406893 -1.4406893

3    C   1  2.9508275  2.9508275  2.9508275

4    D   1 -7.7712261 -7.7712261 -7.7712261

5    E   1 -0.4226972 -0.4226972 -0.4226972

6    F   1 -0.2246766 -0.2246766 -0.2246766

7    G   1 -3.9683617 -3.9683617 -3.9683617

8    H   1 -2.8772308 -2.8772308 -2.8772308

9 Poly   8  8.0702368  8.0702368  8.0702368

N.B. R 3.0.1 plyr 1.8

messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to change the current and future values in one variable based on the current value of another variable. I was able to do it with a for loop, but I'd prefer to do it with plyr or one of the apply functions, because I assume it would be faster (not to mention requiring much less code). However, I haven't been able to make it work in plyr.

Here's a fake data set that has the general features of my data.

grad = structure(list(id = c(5L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 3L, 3L,
3L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), term = structure(c(1L,
2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L,
2L, 3L, 4L), .Label = c("Fall 2011", "Spring 2012", "Fall 2012",
"Spring 2013"), class = c("ordered", "factor")), grad.term = structure(c(NA,
NA, NA, 1L, NA, NA, NA, 1L, NA, 1L, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 1L, NA,
1L, NA, NA), .Label = "Yes", class = "factor"), grad.status = c("Not Graduated",
"Not Graduated", "Not Graduated", "Graduated", "Not Graduated",
"Not Graduated", "Not Graduated", "Graduated", "Not Graduated",
"Graduated", "Graduated", "Graduated", "Not Graduated", "Not Graduated",
"Not Graduated", "Graduated", "Not Graduated", "Graduated", "Graduated",
"Graduated")), .Names = c("id", "term", "grad.term", "grad.status"
), row.names = 21:40, class = "data.frame")

Imagine that we start with just the first three columns (id, term, grad.term). id is a student's identification number; term includes all terms when each student was enrolled; grad.term equals "yes" if a student graduated in that term. I want to create a new variable grad.status (which I've already added to the data set above) which is equal to "Not Graduated" for all terms before the term in which grad.term="Yes", and is equal to "Graduated" for the term in which grad.term="Yes" and all subsequent terms.

Here's what I tried:

# Create a second grad.status variable and initialize all values to "Not Graduated"
grad$grad.status2 =  "Not Graduated"

# For each value of grad$id, if there's a term for which grad.term="Yes", then change the value of grad.status2 to "Graduated" for that term and all future terms.
# The if statement is there to check whether the student graduated. If not, there's no need to change grad.status2 (and trying to do so will cause an error).
ddply(grad, .(id), transform,
    if(length(which(!is.na <http://is.na>(grad.term)))>0) {
        grad.status2[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(grad.term)):length(grad.term)] = "Graduated"
    }
)

The above code doesn't throw an error, but it also doesn't change grad$grad.status2 at all. However, if I limit the data frame to a single value of id, I can check that the basic logic (separate from the plyr command) works:

grad1 = grad[1:4,]
if(which(!is.na <http://is.na>(grad1$grad.term)) {
     grad1$grad.status2[which(!is.na <http://is.na>(grad1$grad.term)):length(grad1$grad.term)] = "Graduated"
     }

I can also make this work in a for loop that loops over the values of id. But, as I said, I'd like to figure out how to do it in plyr. I'm obviously using plyr incorrectly and would appreciate suggestions on how to do it right (along with any suggestions anyone might have on how to improve my overall approach to the problem).

Thanks,
Joel

messages.body_plain:
Here's a way to do it in plyr with a user-written function that is
applied to each id.

g <- function(d)
{
    gradYes <- which(d$grad.term == "Yes")
    gradYes <- if(length(gradYes) > 0) gradYes:nrow(d) else 0
    d[["grad.status"]] <- "Not graduated"
    if(length(gradYes) > 0) d[["grad.status"]][gradYes] <- "Graduated"
    d
}

Let me add on an ungraduated student to verify that it works in that case, too:

grad6 <- data.frame(id = 6, term = c("Fall 2012", "Spring 2013"),
                     grad.term = c(NA, NA))
grad2 <- rbind(grad[, 1:3], grad6)

library(plyr)
ddply(grad2, .(id), g)

messages.subject: ddply with POSIXct (vs. Date)
messages.subject_clean: ddply with POSIXct (vs. Date)
messages.body_plain:
ddply seems to have difficulty with POSIXct. Here is an example (based

on my initial problem, which was using ddply to get ranges of

dates based on a grouping variable. I have omitted a grouping variable here)

try1<-structure(c(-2208988800, -2206310400, -2203891200, -2201212800,

-999475200, -996796800, -994204800, -991526400), class = c("POSIXct",

"POSIXt"), tzone = "UTC")

try1 # all whole dates

# Like try1, but 10-second change to first element

try1a<-structure(c(-2208988800-10, -2206310400, -2203891200, -2201212800,

-999475200, -996796800, -994204800, -991526400), class = c("POSIXct",

"POSIXt"), tzone = "UTC")

try1a[1:4] # 10 second change in first element...

# Like try1, but different class

try2<-structure(c(-25567, -25536, -25508, -25477, -11568, -11537, -11507,

-11476), class = "Date")

all.equal(as.Date(try1),try2)

# put into data frames for ddply use

x1<-data.frame(try1)

x1a<-data.frame(try1a)

x2<-data.frame(try2)

# base R results. These are correct

range(x1$try1)

range(x1a$try1a) # 10 second diff. 1st element is the minimum

range(x2$try2)

# But ...

ddply(x1,.(),function(dfr) range(dfr[,1])) # off by 5 or 4 hours

ddply(x1a,.(),function(dfr) range(dfr[,1])) # delta of 10 secs in min, so delta is correct

ddply(x2,.(),function(dfr) range(dfr[,1])) # OK

# as.Date "corrects" this

ddply(x1,.(),function(dfr) range(as.Date(dfr[,1])))

# and see individual returns values

(test1<-ddply(x1,.(),function(dfr) dfr[1]) )

all.equal(x1,test1[2]) # OK

# But this does not work

ddply(x1,.(),function(dfr) dfr[,1]) # off by 5 or 4 hours

Ideas?

Joe Voelkel
